{"content":"# Thread 1 — SUGGESTION carried into the fix (landed on this branch)

The suggestion asked to prioritize the #1360 fix with the root-cause hint. Done — the fix is now on this branch (`7716bb232`), alongside the (still-active) quarantine entry.

## What the evidence showed

- Both cited gate runs (`37552613207`, `37459648403`) failed with the identical signature: `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` at `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538` — `ws.first` never saw **any** frame after the good-token `hello`.
- The retry-helper "stacking" hypothesis doesn't hold mechanically: `WebSocket.connect` only retries on a **throw**, and with the port pre-bound (`bindLoopback` before boot) pre-listen upgrade requests are **buffered** by the `HttpServer` stream, not refused (verified with a standalone probe). No retries fired in the failing runs — `connect()` returned, so the upgrade completed and `WireServeServer.attach` took the normal path (every other attach path sends a frame the client would have seen).
- The remaining silent-stall site is inside dart:io: `_WebSocketConsumer.add` **drops frames without error** when the upgraded socket's outgoing pipeline is corked (`dart-sdk/lib/_http/websocket_impl.dart`) — a timing wedge, not a security regression, exactly as the review suspected.

## The fix (`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart`)

- `_awaitFirstFrame`: attached-listener wait that records every frame kind and resolves `null` on stream end/error/10s budget (`ws.first` cannot distinguish "slow" from "never").
- On a starved handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the `onDiagnostic` trail for `client detached` (the single-attach gate clears only on the frame stream's `onDone`; if the close frame itself was swallowed by the same corked pipeline, the test fails loudly naming both symptoms instead of a misleading `already_attached`), then **one** fresh-socket handshake retry.
- Phase-1 (bad-token) budget 10s → 20s: it includes the whole boot (the request buffers until the accept loop attaches); 20s is the file's uniform budget.

- E4 green; with the first handshake force-wedged, the retry recovers end-to-end (`client attached` → `client detached` observed by the server → fresh attach → welcome) — the old code hard-fails there with the CI TimeoutException.
- Full `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` (9 tests) + a 30-iteration in-process stress loop over the real `runWireServe`/`httpListen` stack: green.

- The review's one open inline thread (💡 SUGGESTION on `scripts/test_quarantine.json`) verified the quarantine evidence and asked to prioritize the #1360 fix. - The thread's "retry helper stacks pending connections" hypothesis was checked and does not hold mechanically: `WebSocket.connect` retries only on a **throw**, and a pre-bound port buffers pre-listen upgrade requests in the `HttpServer` stream instead of refusing them (verified with a standalone probe). No retries fired in the failing runs — the upgrade completed and `WireServeServer.attach` took its normal path (every other attach path answers with a frame).
- Remaining silent-stall site (SDK source read): dart:io's `_WebSocketConsumer.add` **silently drops** frames when the upgraded socket's outgoing pipeline is corked — the welcome vanishes while the event loop stays alive. A timing wedge, not a security regression — matching the review's own assessment.
- Not reproducible locally (x86): 120+ attempts — single-test loops, full-file runs, concurrent suites under 4-burner CPU saturation — all green; both CI failures were on loaded `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners.
- The quarantine entry itself is untouched and still required: `python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check` passes (7 entries); un-quarantine still needs the AC4 nightly repeat-run proof.

## Approach

Fix landed on this branch (`7716bb232`, test-only; no production code touched):

- `_awaitFirstFrame` helper: an attached-listener wait that records every frame kind and resolves `null` on stream end/error/10s budget — unlike `ws.first`, it distinguishes "slow" from "never" and never hangs.
- On a starved first handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the wire-serve `onDiagnostic` trail for `client detached` (the server's single-attach gate clears only on the frame stream's `onDone`; if the WS close frame itself was swallowed by the same corked pipeline, the test fails loudly naming both symptoms instead of a misleading `already_attached`), then **one** fresh-socket handshake retry — the same tolerance pattern the file's `connect()` helper already applies to boot races.
- Phase-1 (bad-token 401) budget 10s → 20s: it includes the whole boot (the request buffers until the serve closure attaches the accept loop); 20s is the file's uniform budget.

  first = await _awaitFirstFrame(retry, frames);
}

{"command":"git commit -m "test(1360): E4 welcome handshake — one fresh-socket retry gated on the server's detach diagnostic (gh-1360)

CI (2 distinct-SHA gate runs, ubuntu-24.04-arm, loaded) red only on
E4's ws.first.timeout(10s): the welcome frame never arrived after the
good-token hello, while the file's other 8 tests passed in both runs.

Root cause class: dart:io's WebSocket consumer silently drops frames
from a corked outgoing pipeline (_WebSocketConsumer.add returns without
writing when the upgraded socket's addStream controller is closed/corked)
while the event loop stays alive — so the first upgraded socket can lose
the welcome silently and ws.first starves out its whole budget. The
bad-token 401 phase is unaffected (transport-level rejection).

Fix (test-side, like the existing connect() retry helper tolerates boot
races):
- _awaitFirstFrame: attached-listener wait that records every frame kind
  and resolves null on stream end/error/10s budget (ws.first could not
  distinguish 'slow' from 'never').
- On a starved first handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the
  wire-serve onDiagnostic trail for 'client detached' (the single-attach
  gate clears only on the frame stream's onDone, and the WS close frame
  rides the same wedged pipeline — if it was swallowed, fail loudly
  naming both symptoms instead of a misleading already_attached), then
  ONE fresh-socket handshake retry.
- Phase-1 (bad-token) budget 10s -> 20s: it includes the whole boot (the
  request buffers until the serve closure attaches the accept loop);
  20s is the file's uniform budget.

Verified: E4 passes; with the first handshake force-wedged the retry
recovers end-to-end (attach -> detach observed by the server -> fresh
attach -> welcome); full wire_serve file + 30-iteration in-process
stress loop green. Quarantine entry stays until the AC4 nightly

{"content":"# Thread 1 — SUGGESTION carried into the fix (landed on this branch)

The suggestion asked to prioritize the #1360 fix with the root-cause hint. Done — the fix is now on this branch (`7716bb232`), alongside the (still-active) quarantine entry.

## What the evidence showed

- Both cited gate runs (`37552613207`, `37459648403`) failed with the identical signature: `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` at `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538` — `ws.first` never saw **any** frame after the good-token `hello`.
- The retry-helper "stacking" hypothesis doesn't hold mechanically: `WebSocket.connect` only retries on a **throw**, and with the port pre-bound (`bindLoopback` before boot) pre-listen upgrade requests are **buffered** by the `HttpServer` stream, not refused (verified with a standalone probe). No retries fired in the failing runs — `connect()` returned, so the upgrade completed and `WireServeServer.attach` took the normal path (every other attach path sends a frame the client would have seen).
- The remaining silent-stall site is inside dart:io: `_WebSocketConsumer.add` **drops frames without error** when the upgraded socket's outgoing pipeline is corked (`dart-sdk/lib/_http/websocket_impl.dart`) — a timing wedge, not a security regression, exactly as the review suspected.

## The fix (`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart`)

- `_awaitFirstFrame`: attached-listener wait that records every frame kind and resolves `null` on stream end/error/10s budget (`ws.first` cannot distinguish "slow" from "never").
- On a starved handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the `onDiagnostic` trail for `client detached` (the single-attach gate clears only on the frame stream's `onDone`; if the close frame itself was swallowed by the same corked pipeline, the test fails loudly naming both symptoms instead of a misleading `already_attached`), then **one** fresh-socket handshake retry.
- Phase-1 (bad-token) budget 10s → 20s: it includes the whole boot (the request buffers until the accept loop attaches); 20s is the file's uniform budget.

## Verification

- E4 green; with the first handshake force-wedged, the retry recovers end-to-end (`client attached` → `client detached` observed by the server → fresh attach → welcome) — the old code hard-fails there with the CI TimeoutException.
- Full `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` (9 tests) + a 30-iteration in-process stress loop over the real `runWireServe`/`httpListen` stack: green.

The quarantine entry stays until the AC4 nightly repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC6); the nightly now exercises the fixed test supervised.

{"content":"# PR #1361 rework — quarantine entry kept, #1360 flake fix landed on the branch

## Issues/Notes

- The review's one open inline thread (💡 SUGGESTION on `scripts/test_quarantine.json`) verified the quarantine evidence and asked to prioritize the #1360 fix. Both cited gate runs (`37552613207`, `37459648403`) failed with the identical signature: `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000` at `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538` — `ws.first` starved its whole 10s budget with **no** frame after the good-token `hello`, while the file's other 8 tests passed in both runs.
- The thread's "retry helper stacks pending connections" hypothesis was checked and does not hold mechanically: `WebSocket.connect` retries only on a **throw**, and a pre-bound port buffers pre-listen upgrade requests in the `HttpServer` stream instead of refusing them (verified with a standalone probe). No retries fired in the failing runs — the upgrade completed and `WireServeServer.attach` took its normal path (every other attach path answers with a frame).
- Remaining silent-stall site (SDK source read): dart:io's `_WebSocketConsumer.add` **silently drops** frames when the upgraded socket's outgoing pipeline is corked — the welcome vanishes while the event loop stays alive. A timing wedge, not a security regression — matching the review's own assessment.
- Not reproducible locally (x86): 120+ attempts — single-test loops, full-file runs, concurrent suites under 4-burner CPU saturation — all green; both CI failures were on loaded `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners.
- The quarantine entry itself is untouched and still required: `python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check` passes (7 entries); un-quarantine still needs the AC4 nightly repeat-run proof.

## Approach

Fix landed on this branch (`7716bb232`, test-only; no production code touched):

- `_awaitFirstFrame` helper: an attached-listener wait that records every frame kind and resolves `null` on stream end/error/10s budget — unlike `ws.first`, it distinguishes "slow" from "never" and never hangs.
- On a starved first handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the wire-serve `onDiagnostic` trail for `client detached` (the server's single-attach gate clears only on the frame stream's `onDone`; if the WS close frame itself was swallowed by the same corked pipeline, the test fails loudly naming both symptoms instead of a misleading `already_attached`), then **one** fresh-socket handshake retry — the same tolerance pattern the file's `connect()` helper already applies to boot races.
- Phase-1 (bad-token 401) budget 10s → 20s: it includes the whole boot (the request buffers until the serve closure attaches the accept loop); 20s is the file's uniform budget.

```dart
var first = await _awaitFirstFrame(client, frames);
if (first == null) {
  unawaited(client.close().catchError((_) {}));
  expect(await _waitForDiagnostic(diagnostics, 'client detached'), isTrue, ...);
  final retry = await connect(http.port, token: <good token>);
  retry.add(jsonEncode({'v': 1, 'kind': 'hello', 'versions': [1]}));
  first = await _awaitFirstFrame(retry, frames);
}
```

- `test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart` (+102/−6) — E4 handshake hardening + phase-1 budget; committed as `test(1360): E4 welcome handshake — one fresh-socket retry gated on the server's detach diagnostic (gh-1360)`.
- `scripts/test_quarantine.json` — **unchanged**; the entry stays until AC4.

## Test Coverage

- E4 happy path: green (401 on bad token → welcome on good token → token-not-in-records sweep).
- Forced-wedge proof: with the first handshake made to starve, the retry recovers end-to-end — server observes `client attached` → `client detached` → fresh `client attached` → welcome; the old code hard-fails there with the CI `TimeoutException`.
- Full `wire_serve_cli_test.dart` (9 tests) + a 30-iteration in-process stress loop over the real `runWireServe`/`httpListen` stack: green.
- `dart analyze` on the touched file: clean (5 pre-existing style infos elsewhere in the file, present on base).

{"command":"git commit -m "test(1360): E4 welcome handshake — one fresh-socket retry gated on the server's detach diagnostic (gh-1360)

CI (2 distinct-SHA gate runs, ubuntu-24.04-arm, loaded) red only on
E4's ws.first.timeout(10s): the welcome frame never arrived after the
good-token hello, while the file's other 8 tests passed in both runs.

Root cause class: dart:io's WebSocket consumer silently drops frames
from a corked outgoing pipeline (_WebSocketConsumer.add returns without
writing when the upgraded socket's addStream controller is closed/corked)
while the event loop stays alive — so the first upgraded socket can lose
the welcome silently and ws.first starves out its whole budget. The
bad-token 401 phase is unaffected (transport-level rejection).

Fix (test-side, like the existing connect() retry helper tolerates boot
races):
- _awaitFirstFrame: attached-listener wait that records every frame kind
  and resolves null on stream end/error/10s budget (ws.first could not
  distinguish 'slow' from 'never').
- On a starved first handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the
  wire-serve onDiagnostic trail for 'client detached' (the single-attach
  gate clears only on the frame stream's onDone, and the WS close frame
  rides the same wedged pipeline — if it was swallowed, fail loudly
  naming both symptoms instead of a misleading already_attached), then
  ONE fresh-socket handshake retry.
- Phase-1 (bad-token) budget 10s -> 20s: it includes the whole boot (the
  request buffers until the serve closure attaches the accept loop);
  20s is the file's uniform budget.

Verified: E4 passes; with the first handshake force-wedged the retry
recovers end-to-end (attach -> detach observed by the server -> fresh
attach -> welcome); full wire_serve file + 30-iteration in-process
stress loop green. Quarantine entry stays until the AC4 nightly
repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC6)." && git log --oneline -2"}

{"content":"# Thread 1 — SUGGESTION carried into the fix (landed on this branch)

The suggestion asked to prioritize the #1360 fix with the root-cause hint. Done — the fix is now on this branch (`7716bb232`), alongside the (still-active) quarantine entry.

## What the evidence showed

- Both cited gate runs (`37552613207`, `37459648403`) failed with the identical signature: `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` at `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538` — `ws.first` never saw **any** frame after the good-token `hello`.
- The retry-helper "stacking" hypothesis doesn't hold mechanically: `WebSocket.connect` only retries on a **throw**, and with the port pre-bound (`bindLoopback` before boot) pre-listen upgrade requests are **buffered** by the `HttpServer` stream, not refused (verified with a standalone probe). No retries fired in the failing runs — `connect()` returned, so the upgrade completed and `WireServeServer.attach` took the normal path (every other attach path sends a frame the client would have seen).
- The remaining silent-stall site is inside dart:io: `_WebSocketConsumer.add` **drops frames without error** when the upgraded socket's outgoing pipeline is corked (`dart-sdk/lib/_http/websocket_impl.dart`) — a timing wedge, not a security regression, exactly as the review suspected.

## The fix (`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart`)

- `_awaitFirstFrame`: attached-listener wait that records every frame kind and resolves `null` on stream end/error/10s budget (`ws.first` cannot distinguish "slow" from "never").
- On a starved handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the `onDiagnostic` trail for `client detached` (the single-attach gate clears only on the frame stream's `onDone`; if the close frame itself was swallowed by the same corked pipeline, the test fails loudly naming both symptoms instead of a misleading `already_attached`), then **one** fresh-socket handshake retry.
- Phase-1 (bad-token) budget 10s → 20s: it includes the whole boot (the request buffers until the accept loop attaches); 20s is the file's uniform budget.

- E4 green; with the first handshake force-wedged, the retry recovers end-to-end (`client attached` → `client detached` observed by the server → fresh attach → welcome) — the old code hard-fails there with the CI TimeoutException.

- The thread's "retry helper stacks pending connections" hypothesis was checked and does not hold mechanically: `WebSocket.connect` retries only on a **throw**, and a pre-bound port buffers pre-listen upgrade requests in the `HttpServer` stream instead of refusing them (verified with a standalone probe). No retries fired in the failing runs — the upgrade completed and `WireServeServer.attach` took its normal path (every other attach path answers with a frame).
- Remaining silent-stall site (SDK source read): dart:io's `_WebSocketConsumer.add` **silently drops** frames when the upgraded socket's outgoing pipeline is corked — the welcome vanishes while the event loop stays alive. A timing wedge, not a security regression — matching the review's own assessment.
- Not reproducible locally (x86): 120+ attempts — single-test loops, full-file runs, concurrent suites under 4-burner CPU saturation — all green; both CI failures were on loaded `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners.
- The quarantine entry itself is untouched and still required: `python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check` passes (7 entries); un-quarantine still needs the AC4 nightly repeat-run proof.

## Approach

Fix landed on this branch (`7716bb232`, test-only; no production code touched):

- `_awaitFirstFrame` helper: an attached-listener wait that records every frame kind and resolves `null` on stream end/error/10s budget — unlike `ws.first`, it distinguishes "slow" from "never" and never hangs.
- On a starved first handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the wire-serve `onDiagnostic` trail for `client detached` (the server's single-attach gate clears only on the frame stream's `onDone`; if the WS close frame itself was swallowed by the same corked pipeline, the test fails loudly naming both symptoms instead of a misleading `already_attached`), then **one** fresh-socket handshake retry — the same tolerance pattern the file's `connect()` helper already applies to boot races.
- Phase-1 (bad-token 401) budget 10s → 20s: it includes the whole boot (the request buffers until the serve closure attaches the accept loop); 20s is the file's uniform budget.

if (first == null) {

  final retry = await connect(http.port, token: <good token>);

  first = await _awaitFirstFrame(retry, frames);
}

The suggestion asked to prioritize the #1360 fix with the root-cause hint. Done — the fix is now on this branch (`7716bb232`), alongside the (still-active) quarantine entry.

## What the evidence showed

- Both cited gate runs (`37552613207`, `37459648403`) failed with the identical signature: `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` at `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538` — `ws.first` never saw **any** frame after the good-token `hello`.
- The retry-helper "stacking" hypothesis doesn't hold mechanically: `WebSocket.connect` only retries on a **throw**, and with the port pre-bound (`bindLoopback` before boot) pre-listen upgrade requests are **buffered** by the `HttpServer` stream, not refused (verified with a standalone probe). No retries fired in the failing runs — `connect()` returned, so the upgrade completed and `WireServeServer.attach` took the normal path (every other attach path sends a frame the client would have seen).
- The remaining silent-stall site is inside dart:io: `_WebSocketConsumer.add` **drops frames without error** when the upgraded socket's outgoing pipeline is corked (`dart-sdk/lib/_http/websocket_impl.dart`) — a timing wedge, not a security regression, exactly as the review suspected.

- `_awaitFirstFrame`: attached-listener wait that records every frame kind and resolves `null` on stream end/error/10s budget (`ws.first` cannot distinguish "slow" from "never").

- The review's one open inline thread (💡 SUGGESTION on `scripts/test_quarantine.json`) verified the quarantine evidence and asked to prioritize the #1360 fix. No retries fired in the failing runs — the upgrade completed and `WireServeServer.attach` took its normal path (every other attach path answers with a frame).
- Remaining silent-stall site (SDK source read): dart:io's `_WebSocketConsumer.add` **silently drops** frames when the upgraded socket's outgoing pipeline is corked — the welcome vanishes while the event loop stays alive. A timing wedge, not a security regression — matching the review's own assessment.

## Approach

Fix landed on this branch (`7716bb232`, test-only; no production code touched):

- `_awaitFirstFrame` helper: an attached-listener wait that records every frame kind and resolves `null` on stream end/error/10s budget — unlike `ws.first`, it distinguishes "slow" from "never" and never hangs.

- Phase-1 (bad-token 401) budget 10s → 20s: it includes the whole boot (the request buffers until the serve closure attaches the accept loop); 20s is the file's uniform budget.

arguments.message:
## PR #1361 rework complete — quarantine kept, gh-1360 flake fix landed

**Diagnosis** (from both cited CI logs + SDK source + probes): both gate failures are `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000` at `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538` — `ws.first` starved with **zero** frames after the good-token hello. The review's "retry helper stacks connections" hypothesis doesn't hold: `WebSocket.connect` retries only on throw, and a pre-bound port **buffers** pre-listen requests (verified by probe), so no retries fired; `attach()` necessarily took its normal path. The remaining silent-stall site is dart:io's `_WebSocketConsumer.add`, which **silently drops frames from a corked outgoing pipeline** while the event loop stays alive — a timing wedge on loaded `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners, not a security regression (exactly the review's assessment). Not reproducible locally: 120+ attempts (single-test loops, full file, concurrent suites, 4-burner CPU saturation) all green on x86.

**Fix** (`7716bb232`, pushed; test-only, +102/−6 in `test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart`):
- `_awaitFirstFrame`: attached-listener wait recording every frame kind, resolving null on end/error/10s (replaces `ws.first`, which can't tell "slow" from "never").
- On a starved handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the server's `onDiagnostic` trail for `client detached` (the single-attach gate clears only on the frame stream's `onDone`; a swallowed close frame fails loudly naming both symptoms), then **one** fresh-socket handshake retry — the same tolerance pattern as the file's `connect()` helper.
- Phase-1 bad-token budget 10s→20s (it includes the whole boot; 20s is the file's uniform budget).

**Verified**: E4 green; forced-wedge proof shows the retry recovering end-to-end (`attached` → server sees `detached` → fresh attach → welcome) where the old code hard-fails; full wire file + 30-iteration stress loop green; `dart analyze`/`dart format` clean; `apply_quarantine.py --check` passes. Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`) running in background as the regression sweep.

**Quarantine entry unchanged** — stays until the AC4 nightly repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC6); nightly now exercises the fixed test supervised.

**Outputs**: `outputs/response.md`, `outputs/review_replies.json` (thread 1: `inReplyToId` 4202833784, `threadId` `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6pv0eg` verbatim), `outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md`. Threads 2–3 in `pr_discussions_raw.json` carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` (top-level automation comments) — addressed by the fix commit + response.

Also caught and fixed en route: the fa reader redacts secret-like literals (`[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]`) — my first retry-line edit had copied the placeholder, caught via a forced-wedge run that 401'd, repaired via bash byte-exact extraction (both durable lessons saved to project memory).

{"command":"git commit -m "test(1360): E4 welcome handshake — one fresh-socket retry gated on the server's detach diagnostic (gh-1360)

CI (2 distinct-SHA gate runs, ubuntu-24.04-arm, loaded) red only on
E4's ws.first.timeout(10s): the welcome frame never arrived after the
good-token hello, while the file's other 8 tests passed in both runs.

Root cause class: dart:io's WebSocket consumer silently drops frames
from a corked outgoing pipeline (_WebSocketConsumer.add returns without
writing when the upgraded socket's addStream controller is closed/corked)
while the event loop stays alive — so the first upgraded socket can lose
the welcome silently and ws.first starves out its whole budget. The
bad-token 401 phase is unaffected (transport-level rejection).

Fix (test-side, like the existing connect() retry helper tolerates boot
races):
- _awaitFirstFrame: attached-listener wait that records every frame kind
  and resolves null on stream end/error/10s budget (ws.first could not
  distinguish 'slow' from 'never').
- On a starved first handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the
  wire-serve onDiagnostic trail for 'client detached' (the single-attach
  gate clears only on the frame stream's onDone, and the WS close frame
  rides the same wedged pipeline — if it was swallowed, fail loudly
  naming both symptoms instead of a misleading already_attached), then
  ONE fresh-socket handshake retry.
- Phase-1 (bad-token) budget 10s -> 20s: it includes the whole boot (the
  request buffers until the serve closure attaches the accept loop);
  20s is the file's uniform budget.

Verified: E4 passes; with the first handshake force-wedged the retry
recovers end-to-end (attach -> detach observed by the server -> fresh
attach -> welcome); full wire_serve file + 30-iteration in-process
stress loop green. Quarantine entry stays until the AC4 nightly
repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC6)." && git log --oneline -2"}

{"content":"# Thread 1 — SUGGESTION carried into the fix (landed on this branch)

The suggestion asked to prioritize the #1360 fix with the root-cause hint. Done — the fix is now on this branch (`7716bb232`), alongside the (still-active) quarantine entry.

## What the evidence showed

- Both cited gate runs (`37552613207`, `37459648403`) failed with the identical signature: `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000000: Future not completed` at `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538` — `ws.first` never saw **any** frame after the good-token `hello`.
- The retry-helper "stacking" hypothesis doesn't hold mechanically: `WebSocket.connect` only retries on a **throw**, and with the port pre-bound (`bindLoopback` before boot) pre-listen upgrade requests are **buffered** by the `HttpServer` stream, not refused (verified with a standalone probe). No retries fired in the failing runs — `connect()` returned, so the upgrade completed and `WireServeServer.attach` took the normal path (every other attach path sends a frame the client would have seen).
- The remaining silent-stall site is inside dart:io: `_WebSocketConsumer.add` **drops frames without error** when the upgraded socket's outgoing pipeline is corked (`dart-sdk/lib/_http/websocket_impl.dart`) — a timing wedge, not a security regression, exactly as the review suspected.

## The fix (`test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart`)

- `_awaitFirstFrame`: attached-listener wait that records every frame kind and resolves `null` on stream end/error/10s budget (`ws.first` cannot distinguish "slow" from "never").

- Phase-1 (bad-token) budget 10s → 20s: it includes the whole boot (the request buffers until the accept loop attaches); 20s is the file's uniform budget.

No retries fired in the failing runs — the upgrade completed and `WireServeServer.attach` took its normal path (every other attach path answers with a frame).
- Remaining silent-stall site (SDK source read): dart:io's `_WebSocketConsumer.add` **silently drops** frames when the upgraded socket's outgoing pipeline is corked — the welcome vanishes while the event loop stays alive. A timing wedge, not a security regression — matching the review's own assessment.
- Not reproducible locally (x86): 120+ attempts — single-test loops, full-file runs, concurrent suites under 4-burner CPU saturation — all green; both CI failures were on loaded `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners.
- The quarantine entry itself is untouched and still required: `python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check` passes (7 entries); un-quarantine still needs the AC4 nightly repeat-run proof.

## Approach

Fix landed on this branch (`7716bb232`, test-only; no production code touched):

- `_awaitFirstFrame` helper: an attached-listener wait that records every frame kind and resolves `null` on stream end/error/10s budget — unlike `ws.first`, it distinguishes "slow" from "never" and never hangs.
- On a starved first handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the wire-serve `onDiagnostic` trail for `client detached` (the server's single-attach gate clears only on the frame stream's `onDone`; if the WS close frame itself was swallowed by the same corked pipeline, the test fails loudly naming both symptoms instead of a misleading `already_attached`), then **one** fresh-socket handshake retry — the same tolerance pattern the file's `connect()` helper already applies to boot races.
- Phase-1 (bad-token 401) budget 10s → 20s: it includes the whole boot (the request buffers until the serve closure attaches the accept loop); 20s is the file's uniform budget.

```dart
var first = await _awaitFirstFrame(client, frames);
if (first == null) {
  unawaited(client.close().catchError((_) {}));
  expect(await _waitForDiagnostic(diagnostics, 'client detached'), isTrue, ...);
  final retry = await connect(http.port, token: <good token>);
  retry.add(jsonEncode({'v': 1, 'kind': 'hello', 'versions': [1]}));
  first = await _awaitFirstFrame(retry, frames);
}
```

{"message":"## PR #1361 rework complete — quarantine kept, gh-1360 flake fix landed

**Diagnosis** (from both cited CI logs + SDK source + probes): both gate failures are `TimeoutException after 0:00:10.000` at `wire_serve_cli_test.dart:538` — `ws.first` starved with **zero** frames after the good-token hello. The review's "retry helper stacks connections" hypothesis doesn't hold: `WebSocket.connect` retries only on throw, and a pre-bound port **buffers** pre-listen requests (verified by probe), so no retries fired; `attach()` necessarily took its normal path. The remaining silent-stall site is dart:io's `_WebSocketConsumer.add`, which **silently drops frames from a corked outgoing pipeline** while the event loop stays alive — a timing wedge on loaded `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners, not a security regression (exactly the review's assessment). Not reproducible locally: 120+ attempts (single-test loops, full file, concurrent suites, 4-burner CPU saturation) all green on x86.

**Fix** (`7716bb232`, pushed; test-only, +102/−6 in `test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart`):
- `_awaitFirstFrame`: attached-listener wait recording every frame kind, resolving null on end/error/10s (replaces `ws.first`, which can't tell "slow" from "never").
- On a starved handshake: close the wedged socket, poll the server's `onDiagnostic` trail for `client detached` (the single-attach gate clears only on the frame stream's `onDone`; a swallowed close frame fails loudly naming both symptoms), then **one** fresh-socket handshake retry — the same tolerance pattern as the file's `connect()` helper.
- Phase-1 bad-token budget 10s→20s (it includes the whole boot; 20s is the file's uniform budget).

**Verified**: E4 green; forced-wedge proof shows the retry recovering end-to-end (`attached` → server sees `detached` → fresh attach → welcome) where the old code hard-fails; full wire file + 30-iteration stress loop green; `dart analyze`/`dart format` clean; `apply_quarantine.py --check` passes. Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`) running in background as the regression sweep.

**Quarantine entry unchanged** — stays until the AC4 nightly repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC6); nightly now exercises the fixed test supervised.
